title: Book One · Chapter 32: Up
story:
On Thursday afternoon, Mum takes the boys to the drying yard. The gate is open. The woman with the baskets says the far half is free until the evening cart comes.

"The broken tiles are still in that corner," she says.

"We remember," Leo says.

They put the board in the safe half. Mum sits on the low step. She can see the whole space from there. The wind moves past in short warm pushes.

Ronan marks the first position of the meeting knot. Leo checks the patch. It is dry.

The first try lasts hardly longer than the others. The kite rises, leans, and drops.

Ronan catches his breath. He looked forward to this try. The kite had new lines. He wanted it to fly. But the kite fell again. He looks at the paper. He says nothing yet.

"No tear," Leo reports.

They move the meeting knot a small distance and mark the new place. The tail stays in the middle. The string stays short.

This time, Leo holds the line. Ronan lifts the kite into the breeze. The paper pushes against his hands. He lets go.

The kite goes up.

The wind lifts it. The kite turns a little, then stays up. Its blue tail shakes below it. Leo's shoulders go high with his hands.

"Don't pull all at once!" Ronan calls.

"I'm not!"

Leo takes one step backward. The kite stays up. It is above Mum's head, above the wall, and still whole.

Ronan's mouth opens. For once, he has no words ready. The brown shape is not the beautiful red kite in the picture. It has a dark mark, a paper patch, and the tail of three blues. He can see their new lines, their patch, and their tail.

"It works," he says at last.

Mum stands. She doesn't tell them to pose or make a speech. She says, "I can see."

The wind weakens. The kite begins to lower. Leo wants to run, but there is only a little safe ground left.

"Walk it down," Mum says.

Ronan moves forward and catches the frame before it drags. Both boys breathe out loudly.

"How long?" Leo asks.

"I didn't count."

"Long enough."

They sit beside the board. Leo points to the new line mark. "It flew from here," he says. Ronan draws one blue up arrow. He makes it bigger than the down arrows, then rubs part out. It has to leave room for the date.

They try again. This time, Ronan holds the line. The kite rises, but not as high. A sudden breeze pushes it sideways. He lets the card move a little in his hand. He takes one step. The string stops pulling so hard.

The kite moves with the wind. Ronan watches it as he holds the line. He leaves room to step sideways. He does not pull every time the kite turns.

Leo asks to let more string out. Ronan looks at the yard. The cart gate is close, and there is a roof beyond the wall.

"Not here. This is good."

Leo looks up. "All right."

They bring the kite down when the woman calls from the gate. The evening cart is coming. Both boys help bring it down. They stop before the cart comes in. Ronan puts the kite on the board. He is still smiling.

At home, Dad hears their feet. He comes to the door. Both boys begin at once.

"One voice," Mum says.

They stop. Then Ronan holds up the page. Dad sees the blue arrow. He smiles before either boy speaks again.

---

重点表达：rises＝升起；patch＝补片；frame＝框架；backward＝向后。

理解问题：

1. 哪次调整后，风筝终于稳定飞起？
2. 两人为什么没有立刻把线全放出去？
